l2_curated_knowledge.content: APT29 is known to use compromised infrastructure and valid accounts to maintain persistence.
T1110 - Brute Force: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt access to accounts when passwords are unknown.
T1548 - Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevate privileges to gain higher-level permissions.
IP 185.20.10.1 is a known command and control (C2) server associated with multiple recent campaigns.

rag_knowledge_documents.title: Unauthorized privileged access
rag_knowledge_documents.text: Unauthorized privileged access can indicate privilege escalation or misuse of administrative credentials. Investigate which account elevated, from which host, and whether the elevation matches an approved change.

rag_knowledge_documents.title: Valid Accounts
rag_knowledge_documents.text: Valid Accounts is a MITRE ATT&CK technique involving the use of legitimate credentials to gain access. Adversaries reuse stolen credentials so their activity blends in with normal authentication traffic.

rag_knowledge_documents.title: Baseline authentication behaviour
rag_knowledge_documents.text: Normal authentication events do not necessarily indicate malicious activity. A single successful login from a known host and a usual time window is expected behaviour and should not be escalated on its own.

rag_knowledge_documents.title: Brute Force
rag_knowledge_documents.text: Brute Force covers repeated authentication attempts against one or many accounts. A burst of failures from a single source IP followed by a success is a strong indicator of a successful password guessing attack.

rag_knowledge_documents.title: Command and control traffic
rag_knowledge_documents.text: Outbound traffic to a known command and control server suggests an already compromised host. Isolate the host and review what was transferred before the connection was observed.

rag_knowledge_documents.title: UAC bypass
rag_knowledge_documents.text: Windows User Account Control bypasses let a process run with elevated integrity without prompting the user. Look for auto-elevating binaries and unusual parent-child process chains.
